articles.title: GM plans ‘eyes-off’ driving for most popular selling SUVs, trucks
articles.desc:
GM plans to extend “eyes-off” autonomous highway driving beyond its EV lineup to its gas-powered vehicles, including full-size SUVs and light-duty pickups, in upcoming years, according to a press release .

“The promise of personal autonomy is giving people their time back,” the release states. “By pairing our centralized compute architecture with rigorous real-world validation, GM is moving from an initial limited debut to widespread availability across our most popular trucks and SUVs, making trusted autonomy available to everyday drivers.”

The automaker announced last year that it would launch “eyes-off” autonomous highway driving on its Cadillac ESCALADE IQ in 2028. It plans to expand the technology to its highest-volume and best-selling vehicle lineups following the Cadillac ESCALADE IQ.

“Our vision is to build vehicles that can drive themselves or their occupants anywhere they need to be,” the release states. “This includes a future where your vehicle can handle mundane tasks for you, like heading out into bumper-to-bumper traffic to pick up groceries or dry cleaning, giving you valuable time back.”

Reuters reports that, currently, GM’s Super Cruise and Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised) control steering and speed in certain settings. It adds the systems can sometimes be hands-free but require the driver to remain attentive.

Only a few automakers have introduced eyes-off systems, including Mercedes-Benz. However, service typically is limited to small geographic areas at low speeds, according to the article.

GM points to its new central compute architecture that decouples software from physical hardware as one advancement that helps it push autonomy forward.

“It’s designed to provide a common computing, network, software, and interface foundation across a broad portfolio while allowing each vehicle to retain the hardware and controls required for its specific purpose,” the release adds.

A liquid-cooled central compute unit (CCU) is another advancement.

GM says it has 40 times more compute capability, which can support AI and autonomy. It adds that the computing hub consolidates autonomy, active safety, chassis, and propulsion software onto a single, high-speed core.

articles.title: Entegral and GEICO partner for automotive claims process

He gave other examples of ADAS sublets and paint, parts, and equipment providers.

articles.title: Autel software update gains access to Nissan’s restricted CONSULT 4 vehicle line
articles.desc:
Nissan’s CONSULT 4 vehicle line secures access to critical vehicle systems, but Autel says it has gained access for ADAS calibrations and other services.

A news release from Autel says that available functions include ECU information, code reading and clearing, live data, active tests and ADAS calibration procedures, depending on the vehicle.

The software gives access to protected vehicle functions through AutoAuth, the release adds.

“Our current licensing covers data and all current secure gateway access,” Paul A. Marshall, Autel director of product development, told Repairer Driven News (RDN). “This includes AutoAuth and the MAC Keys Auth licensing process to access secured Body Control Modules.”

Marshall said this access is necessary to calibrate some 2025 and 2026 Nissan vehicles.

“We worked with Nissan U.S. and Japan to validate our process,” Marshall said.

The Equipment and Tool Institute (ETI) manages Autel’s Nissan licensing, Marshall further explained. He said ETI worked directly with Nissan during the process.

Allison A. Whitney, Autel’s director of corporate communications, told RDN that Nissan provided security-access information and reviewed diagnostic logs supplied by Autel. She adds that the automaker also provided guidance on accessing protected vehicle control modules and that in specific logs, Nissan confirmed successful security access and command transmission.

Whitney noted that “technical assistance is distinct from Nissan’s endorsement or certification of Autel products.”

Nissan’s technical review of particular access sequences and diagnostic logs should not be interpreted as product-wide validation, Whitney said.

“Approval for a dealer equipment program is also a separate matter,” Whitney said.

She adds that Autel is pursuing approval for its IA1000 through that process and approval is pending.

Autel’s diagnostic software for Nissan is available on MaxiSYS Ultra and Ultra S2 tablets, Autel’s release states. The ADAS calibration capabilities are available on Ultra and Ultra S2 series tablets with ADAS calibration software.

“On newer Nissan platforms, security-gateway restrictions previously prevented aftermarket diagnostic tools from accessing certain protected functions, including code clearing, Active Tests, and ADAS calibration procedures,” said Vinie Putrino, Autel senior testing specialist, during a live demonstration at Auto Glass Week 2026, according to the release. “This expanded access gives Autel users the ability to perform supported diagnostic and calibration functions through the established AutoAuth authorization process.”

The release notes that Nissan began incorporating security-gateway protections into select North American vehicles with the 2020 model year. The protections restrict access to designated bidirectional functions unless the technician, shop, and diagnostic tool are properly authenticated.

Autel has offered AutoAuth-based Nissan security-gateway access for several years on applicable vehicles supported by Nissan’s CONSULT-III plus diagnostic platform, according to the release.

CONSULT 4, Nissan’s newer web-based diagnostic software, was introduced for the 2023 Nissan Ariya and is now on a growing number of newer Nissan vehicle platforms, the release states. It adds that supporting functions on these vehicles required Autel to develop and validate a reliable authorization process compatible with newer electronic architectures.

Whitney says that AutoAuth provided the authentication and authorization process used to obtain secure access to protected Nissan vehicle functions with compatible aftermarket tools. She adds that it connects eligible shops, users, and tools with Nissan’s security access process.

Whitney describes the access as the breadth of supported bidirectional functions beyond reading fault codes and live data.

“Bidirectional capability allows the tool to send commands to the vehicle — for example, to activate a component for testing or initiate a supported ADAS calibration routine,” Whitney said. “Coverage varies by vehicle, control module, and procedure. articles.title: A proposed federal bill could put auto sellers in prison for not disclosing missing, disabled airbags
articles.desc:
U.S. Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY-District 17) has filed a bill that would require auto dealerships and other resale channels selling used vehicles to sell them with functional airbag systems, or, if an airbag is missing or disabled, to clearly disclose that.

If passed, the bill would mean up to life in prison for sellers if someone dies as a result of a vehicle sold at an auction or dealership without disclosing the vehicle is missing an airbag or is equipped with a disabled one.

Lawler filed the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act this week, according to a press release from his office .

Anthony Amoros died in 2013 at the age of 18 after crashing his car on a windy stretch of road, according to a New York CBS News report . Amoros’s family purchased the vehicle without knowing it lacked an airbag.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a bill titled “Anthony Amoros Law” in 2021 that prohibits used car dealers from selling vehicles without a working airbag, according to Spectrum News . The law requires sellers to provide consumers with certification that the vehicle is equipped with an airbag.

“Every driver and passenger deserves to know that the vehicle they are getting into is safe, and this bill will help protect consumers by making sure they have the information they need to make informed decisions,” Lawler said in his press release. “This legislation will ensure dealerships and third-party sellers cannot sell these vehicles without clearly informing consumers of the safety risks.”

Lawler’s bill would require sellers to disclose that vehicles don’t have a working airbag on the front of the sales contract receipt and invoice.

The proposed law would give state officials or agencies authority to regulate and enforce compliance after Federal Trade Commission (FTC) notice.

The FTC will have the right to intervene in any action or file a petition of appeal.

Penalties outlined in the bill allow for a court to award an additional $25,000 for an action that involves death or paralysis.

The bill states that those who knowingly sell a vehicle without a working airbag and disclosure could be fined and face up to 10 years in prison.

It adds that a seller could face up to 20 years in prison if someone is seriously injured, including paralysis.

The bill also defines a “deficiency” as a vehicle without a functional airbag system and/or inflatable restraint system.

Counterfeit airbags are not specifically mentioned in the bill. However, it’s likely that vehicles without an airbag or a deficient airbag system travel through the same salvage routes as vehicles with counterfeit airbags.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recently identified an 11th death caused by a counterfeit airbag part that the agency banned earlier this year .

The death happened Aug. 27 in Dallas, Texas, and is described as an otherwise survivable crash by NHTSA.

Teena Bohi, an Automotive Anti-Counterfeiting Council (A2C2) board member, said during a Collision Industry Conference (CIC) meeting in July that NHTSA’s investigation has uncovered how dangerous counterfeit parts find their way into vehicles.

“The totaling of a vehicle isn’t a cut-and-dried process,” Bohi says. “The value is driven depending on whether it is self-insured, the state the vehicle was in, the insurer’s own practices, processes, and thresholds. There is a lot that goes into just determining if the vehicle is totaled.”

Next, the vehicle often goes to an auction. If it is a public auction, an airbag deployment will possibly be reported to the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System (NMVTIS). The system is a database meant to prevent the resale of stolen vehicles and track unsafe salvage cars. If the vehicle goes to a wholesale or private auction, the previous crash information is not always captured, she said.

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 75 ft./lbs.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Be careful as you retract the piston.

After the pads are replaced, pump the pedal and adjust the parking brake mechanism in the rear calipers. If the level has too much travel, perform the following steps:

Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

The biggest ABS issue with the three generations of Mazda 3 is power. With some higher mileage vehicles, the battery cables, wiring from the power distribution box or the ground connection (behind the driver’s side headlight at G02) can have enough resistance so the voltage drops below 8 volts. When this happens, the ABS module cuts control and the electronic brake distribution system is disabled.

If a modulator/control unit is replaced, the pressure sensors must be recalibrated with a scan tool that is able to communicate with the chassis/ABS module. If this is not performed, it can result in brake failure and lock up.

If you have DTCs C1141, C1142, C1143, C1144, C1233, C1234, C1235 or C1236 (ABS wheel-speed sensor/ABS sensor rotor), chances are something is wrong with the wheel bearings. articles.title: Brake Job: 2019-Present Ram 2500
articles.desc:
The fifth-generation Ram 2500 places substantial demands on its brakes. Many of these trucks carry heavy payloads, tow trailers or operate in fleets, so a successful brake job requires a complete-system inspection and parts that match the platform’s thermal and mechanical demands.

- Modern Maintenance Requires More Than Checking Mileage

This Brake Job covers the 2019-present fifth-generation Ram 2500, not the Ram 1500. The 2500 uses heavy-duty components and platform-specific procedures. Confirm the model year, engine, axle and options before ordering parts or applying specifications.

The Ram 2500 has four-wheel vented discs and dual-piston sliding calipers. Separate parking-brake shoes act against a drum surface inside each rear rotor hat.

Booster configuration depends on the engine. The 6.4L Hemi uses a dual-diaphragm vacuum booster and an electric vacuum pump near the left front of the engine to supplement engine vacuum. The PCM commands the pump based on operating inputs. The 6.7L diesel uses Hydro-Boost, supplied by the power-steering pump, with an accumulator providing limited reserve assist if pump pressure is lost.

When it’s practical, begin the process with a road test and note pedal travel, assist, pull, vibration and noise under normal braking. Confirm the complaint before disassembly; a vibration blamed on the front brakes may originate at the rear, and an assist complaint may come from the vacuum or power-steering circuit rather than the foundation brakes.

Clean around the master-cylinder cap and verify that the fluid is at the MAX mark. On a diesel vehicle, you should also inspect the power-steering fluid level, hoses and lines, because Hydro-Boost depends on that circuit. Low fluid, leaks, restrictions or weak pump output can create assist complaints. On gasoline models, inspect booster vacuum plumbing and electric-pump operation.

Compare inner and outer pad wear and both sides of each axle. Uneven wear can reveal seized hardware, binding pads, piston trouble or slide problems. Replace pads as an axle set if usable lining at the thinnest point is 1 mm (0.04 inch) or less. Inspect boots, pistons, slides, hoses and bleeders for damage, leakage and corrosion.

Be sure to measure the rotors. Minimum thickness is 37.4 mm (1.47 inches) front and 32.4 mm (1.28 inches) rear. Maximum runout is 0.020 mm (0.0008 inch); maximum loose-rotor thickness variation is 0.008 mm (0.00031 inch). You should also inspect the internal parking-brake surface; maximum drum diameter is 207.2 mm (8.157 inches).

Support the caliper and adapter; never let the hose carry their weight. Clean the pad lands and hub face without removing base metal. Install new anti-rattle clips, verify free pad movement and make sure both pistons retract smoothly. Because the rotor fits over the hub studs, hub cleanliness and uniform wheel-fastener torque are critical to controlling installed runout.

Rear service adds the parking-brake assembly. A rotor that will not release may be hanging on the shoes, so release the pedal and back off the star wheel if necessary. With the rotor off, inspect the shoes, springs, adjuster, cable action and drum surface. Clean the hub and bracket, verify piston and slide movement, and install new hardware and sealing washers as required.

Always replace caliper hardware; old clips can restrict pad movement and cause uneven wear.

Use fresh fluid meeting SAE J1703-F and DOT 3 standards. Bleed in this order: right rear, left rear, right front and left front, keeping the reservoir full. For pressure bleeding, use the correct adapter; 15-20 PSI is generally sufficient, depending on equipment limits.

If air entered the HCU, perform a base bleed, use a capable scan tool’s ABS Miscellaneous menu to run the HCU bleed routine, then bleed the base system again. Set the fluid level and verify a firm pedal.

Hydro-Boost is generally self- bleeding. Fill the power-steering reservoir, disable the engine and crank it for several seconds, then recheck the level. Re-enable and start the engine, slowly turn lock to lock twice, shut it off and discharge the accumulator with five pedal applications. Restart, repeat two slow lock-to-lock cycles, shut down and correct the level. If the fluid foams, let it dissipate before repeating the final cycles.

Adjust the shoes before cable tension. With the pedal fully released and the front cable slackened at the frame-rail adjuster, turn each star wheel through the backing-plate hole until slight drag is felt, then back it off until drag disappears. Adjust both sides equally.

Cable-tensioner adjustment is normally required only after replacement or disconnection. After verifying cable movement and shoe adjustment, fully apply the pedal. Mark the non-threaded tensioner rod 1/4 inch from the tensioner edge and tighten the nut until the mark disappears. Release the pedal, confirm both wheels rotate freely, verify that the brake holds and road-test the truck.

articles.title: Recalling The Brake Rotor Wars of the Early 2000s
articles.desc:
Last year, Chinese and Turkish brake drum manufacturers were hit with antidumping duties for selling some trailer brake drums in the United States at less than fair market value. The news gave me flashbacks to the light-vehicle  rotor market 25 years ago, when I first started working on Brake & Front End magazine.

- A Look at the Multi-Functional Clutch 1 in Nissan’s CVT

In the early 2000s, shops faced brake pedal pulsation comebacks for several reasons. Some people might call it a perfect storm.

Facing new fuel-efficiency standards, OEMs began removing mass from brake rotors. Vehicles such as the Jeep Cherokee and Chevrolet Malibu used “composite” rotor designs with stamped-steel hats cast into iron friction rings. These rotors  would develop lateral runout if the lug nuts were tightened even slightly unevenly.

Some rotor manufacturers introduced one-piece replacements for these composite applications, but wheel-stud length was always a concern. Because the cast hats were thicker, the studs sometimes did not extend far enough beyond the rotor flange to properly secure the wheel. Some aftermarket brake companies even offered longer wheel-stud kits.

This period also marked the infancy of ceramic brake pad formulations. Most OE friction materials at the start of the transition process were semi-metallic or aggressive non-asbestos organic (NAO) compounds that could contribute to disc thickness variation when even a small amounts of runout were present. Ceramic formulations were being rolled out that on new OE platforms and as aftermarket alternatives. They can be credited, at least in part, with extending rotor life and reducing incidents of brake pedal pulsation.

What I remember most was the debate surrounding replacement brake rotors. In the late 1990s, “offshore manufacturers” were selling brake rotors at prices well below fair market value. By 2006, the federal government had begun investigating the situation and imposed antidumping duties on certain imports.

Within the aftermarket, some brake brands alleged that these inexpensive rotors were unsafe. Their main argument was that manufacturers were reducing rotor weight by making the friction plates thinner and failing to match the original fin design. I remember several press events that highlighted these design differences. I also remember phone calls from other rotor manufacturers arguing that the practice was acceptable because OE rotors were designed with an “eight-times” safety margin.

The lasting effect of these events were on technicians and repair shops. Replacement brake rotors became so inexpensive that installing new ones often cost less than the labor required to machine the originals. The economics allowed shops to recommend new rotors with increasing frequency, based on the rationale that replacement produced a more reliable, comeback-free brake job.

This replacement mindset even prompted California’s Bureau of Automotive Repair to conduct a sting investigation in 2010 targeting shops that recommended new rotors without first measuring the thickness of the existing ones.

Like it or not, we have been spoiled by inexpensive brake rotors over the past 20 years. Their availability permanently changed how some technicians and shops service brake systems. Today, it is not uncommon for technicians to recommend new rotors regardless of whether the existing rotors remain within specification, based on the economics.

The market, however, is always changing. Vehicle brake systems have improved, and modern friction formulations have extended rotor life through better ceramic transfer-layer developments. OEMs have also increased the size and mass of many brake rotors to improve braking performance, manage heat and control noise.

On the parts side, replacement rotor prices have increased because of higher transportation costs, inflation, tariffs and other market pressures. Rotors have also become more sophisticated, incorporating improved hat and heat-dam designs. Coatings and treatments such as ferritic nitrocarburizing have further increased the price of replacement rotors.

In my opinion, we are approaching another perfect storm. As replacement rotor prices rise and original brake rotors become more durable, the economics of replacement versus machining are beginning to converge on some brake jobs—especially when shops compare labor and parts costs while accounting for the rotor’s discard dimension.

As an industry veteran who survived the rotor wars, I see this as a win-win for repair shops. On the labor side, machining rotors can be a profitable again. On the parts side, selling a higher-value replacement rotor can generate more gross-profit dollars.

It may be time to dust off your micrometers and tune up your brake lathes.

articles.desc:
Drawing on its experience developing and industrializing fuel cell technology, EKPO is advancing hydrogen use across various mobility applications. The HyFleet project illustrates how this technology can support demanding specialty vehicle applications. EKPO’s high-performance NM12 stack forms the heart of the fuel cell system. The stack delivers high power density and supports the 90-kW fuel cell system. The system achieves an efficiency of up to 60% and responds rapidly to changes in load.

Extensive on- and off-road testing under real-world conditions demonstrates the system’s suitability for practical use.

EKPO collaborated with HyCentA to develop a passive hydrogen recirculation system that provides additional robustness and efficiency. An innovative two-step needle ejector reduces mechanical complexity.

The system also supports cold starts and freeze starts at temperatures as low as minus 20 degrees Celsius. These capabilities allow operation in winter and alpine conditions.

“HyFleet shows how we are applying our many years of fuel cell expertise to new mobility applications,” said Dr. Stefan Dwenger, managing director of EKPO Fuel Cell Technologies GmbH. “Hydrogen is particularly well suited to demanding on- and off-road applications that require long operating hours and high availability. Our NM12 fuel cell stack, backed by our expertise in development and industrialization, helps our partners put this potential to work.”

HyFleet Tests Hydrogen Applications Under Real-World Conditions

The HyFleet initiative tests this technology under real-world operating conditions. The project generates insights into hydrogen-powered specialty vehicles for agriculture, forestry, tourism, municipal services and industry, among other sectors.

HyFleet takes an integrated approach to operating hydrogen-powered vehicle fleets. The project considers every stage, from local green hydrogen production to the powertrain, vehicle and scalable refueling infrastructure. The results also help guide further development and the technology’s use in additional applications.

“HyFleet has demonstrated that a hydrogen fuel cell powertrain can also work successfully in a compact special-purpose vehicle designed for off-road use,” said Stefan Arndt, general manager BRP-Rotax, VP R&D Powertrain. “In EKPO, we have a partner that brought extensive experience in developing and industrializing fuel cell stacks to the project, along with technology tailored to our needs. EKPO thus played a key role in turning our vehicle concept into reality.”

EKPO brings more than 20 years of fuel cell technology experience to its development and industrialization capabilities. The company draws on its automotive industry experience to develop fuel cell solutions. Alongside HyFleet, EKPO will showcase fuel cell stacks and components for mobile and stationary applications at the event in Hamburg.

The modular platforms offer power outputs ranging from 16 kW to more than 400 kW. Their designs emphasize high power density, efficiency and reliable operation. EKPO also develops customized stack solutions that meet each customer’s system architecture and specific requirements.

EKPO’s portfolio extends to green hydrogen production. The company develops and manufactures metal bipolar plates for proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers. EKPO applies its expertise in precision forming, coating and sealing technologies to meet the specific demands of electrolysis. The company designs the bipolar plates to withstand demanding operating conditions and support scalable industrial manufacturing.

articles.title: Schaeffler Offers Aftermarket Parts for Toyota, Ford Hybrids
articles.desc:
The Schaeffler division is making two Vitesco repair solutions available to the automotive aftermarket: a Voltage Stabilization System (VSS) for micro hybrid vehicles from Toyota and Peugeot S.A. (PSA), and a 48V DC/DC converter for Ford mild hybrid vehicles.

- Preventing EV Lithium-ion Battery Fires

- Charging and Replacing Batteries with Advanced Power Management Systems

The VSS is available immediately. According to Schaeffler, it prevents voltage drops that can occur during automatic start-stop operation in micro-hybrid vehicles. The system consists of an Energy Storage System (ESS) with high-performance capacitors and a Power Electronics Unit (PEU).

Schaeffler notes that during the engine start process, the capacitors release energy stored while driving within a very short time, compensating for the high-power demand. Starting the engine via a starter-generator requires a comparatively high amount of energy.

If this energy is drawn solely from the conventional 12-volt electrical system, the voltage can briefly drop by several volts, causing visible flickering of the vehicle’s lighting and electronic displays. Schaeffler said that by stabilizing the voltage supply, the capacitors ensure smooth engine restarting and contribute to longer battery life, improved driving comfort and compliance with current emissions standards.

The Schaeffler Vitesco 48V DC/DC converter, available in May, is used in mild-hybrid vehicles equipped with a 48V starter generator and an additional battery to enable more efficient power delivery and boost performance during acceleration, the company says. The converter links the vehicle’s 48-volt electrical system with the 12-volt onboard electronics.

The converter is a component of energy management in mild-hybrid vehicles and for achieving type-approval compliant CO2 emissions. Its bidirectional design allows 12-volt components to be supplied from the 48-volt network while charging the starter battery. Conversely, in the event of a temporary failure, the 48-volt system can also draw energy from the 12-volt network, the company notes.

articles.title: 31.08.2026 Press release Smart Home Ten Years of Bosch Smart Home Stuttgart / Berlin – For ten years, Bosch Smart Home has been developing solutions for a connected home designed around residents’ genuine needs. What began as individual smart devices has evolved into a comprehensive system that combines convenience, security, and intuitive everyday control. Bosch Smart Home stands for high quality, reliability, and robust data protection. True to Bosch’s slogan “Invented for life,” the technology delivers real value by making daily life noticeably easier and giving people more time for what truly matters. At IFA 2026, Bosch Smart Home is showcasing innovations that enhance living comfort, make heating more responsive to actual needs, and simplify life via intelligent security features.Home+ gains key new functions The existing optional Home+ service – which already included multisystem control, expanded cloud storage, and intelligent noise detection – has been expanded to include two attractive new indoor climate features: Optimised Heat Distribution and Demand-Optimised Heating. Home+ thus integrates even more key functions for comfort, accurately targeted heating, and system control into a single, expanded service. The price remains unchanged at €4.99 per month. Optimised Heat Distribution for greater efficiency and comfort In many households, heat is not distributed evenly: radiators near the heating circuit pump often receive too much flow, while more distantly situated radiators do not get enough heat. The unwanted consequences are imbalanced temperatures, unnecessary energy consumption, and annoying flow noise within the heating system. This is precisely where the new Bosch Smart Home solution comes in: the Smart Radiator Thermostats II [+M] automate hydronic balancing and continuously optimise heat distribution. The system analyses heating operation in real time to ensure that each radiator consistently receives exactly the required amount of heat. The results are rooms with uniform temperatures, fewer common heating problems (e.g., chilly or overheated rooms), reduced energy consumption, and quieter operation. The solution thus provides long-lasting comfort and efficiency – entirely without manual intervention. Demand-Optimised Heating for intelligent energy management Even with optimal heat distribution, many heating systems consume more energy than is actually required, resulting in inefficient operation. A demand-optimised control system solves this problem by directly connecting individual thermostats to the central heat generator. Linking heat pumps (via Bosch Connect Key K40 or Buderus MX400) with smart radiator thermostats or 230V room thermostats enables predictive heating behaviour. Precise and dynamic adjustment of the flow temperature means heat is generated only when it is actually needed. This achieves optimised heat-pump utilization and accurately targeted energy consumption. Integration into the smart home unlocks further potential for savings: customised schedules and automation routines support demand-based heating control. At the same time, living comfort remains fully supported because each room’s temperature can be set individually and implemented automatically. This makes the entire heating system more efficient, striking a perfect balance between comfort and optimised energy consumption. The whole heating system – even one with multiple heating circuits – can be controlled centrally via a single app, thus ensuring intuitive operation and complete transparency. When paired with a compatible Bosch or Buderus heat pump, the system offers an additional convenient feature: active cooling via underfloor heating on warm days. Additionally, a special version of the Radiator Thermostat II [+M] PRO is available. The model is distributed and installed exclusively by professional installers. With this variant, the Optimised Heat Distribution and Demand-Optimised Heating functions are permanently enabled by default during the installation process. Particularly attractive for end customers: the total costs of this optimisation measure – including hardware and professional installation – are eligible for subsidy under the Federal Funding for Efficient Buildings (BEG) programme. Eyes+: the smart camera upgrade with intelligent person recognition Bosch Smart Home has enhanced its camera portfolio with “Eyes+”, a feature offering intelligent person recognition. This function is available as an add-on service for all Bosch Smart Home indoor and outdoor cameras. Eyes+ automatically distinguishes between known and unknown individuals: it notifies users only in case of truly relevant events, thus preventing a distracting deluge of unnecessary alerts. During the one-time-only setup process, the system captures multiple images of a person’s head from various angles. An algorithm uses these images to generate an encrypted digital feature profile. This data is securely stored in the Bosch Cloud and cannot be reconstructed into an image. The profile serves solely to differentiate between known and unknown persons. Captured images are subsequently deleted, with the exception of a single image retained to display the known person within the app. This supports the accurately targeted filtering of relevant events, thus ensuring that only genuinely important push notifications are sent. A preview image in the app enables users to promptly assess each situation at a glance. In the event of unusual activity, users can react immediately, if necessary, thereby enjoying a greater sense of everyday security. Additionally, Eyes+ provides greater transparency and peace of mind in everyday family life, for example by sending a notification as soon as loved ones arrive home. Ten years of Bosch Smart Home: evolution into an integrated system With its new product launches at IFA 2026, Bosch Smart Home showcases the further development of its system over the past decade: an evolutionary journey from individual connected devices to an integrated, comprehensive solution that optimises comfort and security, thus giving users the confidence of knowing that everything at home is functioning reliably. New capabilities for indoor climate, energy usage, and home security demonstrate how state-of-the-art technology can deliver accurately targeted support and provide genuine value in daily life. For users, this means less effort and more time for what really matters – thanks to a home where they feel truly at ease. Availability and pricing Home+, including the “Optimised Heat Distribution” and “Demand-Optimised Heating” extensions, is available in the Bosch Smart Home app for €4.99 per month (incl. 19% VAT). The Radiator Thermostat II [+M] PRO will be available directly from installers starting in September 2026. The “Eyes+ Intelligent Person Recognition” feature can be added via the Bosch Smart Camera app starting in November 2026 for €2.99 per month (incl. 19% VAT).

articles.title: 15.09.2026 Press release Mobility Industry leaders scale full value chain for hydrogen mobility across Europe Stuttgart / Hannover – Today at IAA Transportation, Volvo Group, Daimler Truck, Toyota Motor Corporation, Bosch, Air Liquide, TotalEnergies, TEAL Mobility, and MB Energy unveiled their plans to accelerate the rollout of hydrogen-powered vehicles across Europe. For the first time in Europe, the German ecosystem has put in place all the conditions for a scalable deployment of Hydrogen trucks by 2030, driven by the German authorities and European industrial leaders along the value chain. Building on the German deployment model as a practical baseline, scaling these solutions across the continent calls for aligned support from national governments and the European Commission to ensure long-term energy resilience and competitiveness.Rooted in the shared conviction that hydrogen is an important complement to battery-electric vehicles in achieving the EU’s decarbonization targets, industry leaders are joining forces to overcome historical bottlenecks, particularly for truck operations requiring long range, high payload capacity, rapid refueling and operational flexibility. At Daimler Truck, customers have driven almost 600,000 kilometers with fuel cell trucks. As the next step, the company plans to deploy a small series of 100 next generation fuel cell trucks into customer operations from the end of 2026 onwards. In parallel, the first hydrogen combustion engine trucks are being prepared for market launch next year. Overall, the company invests a mid-three-digit million euro amount in hydrogen trucks by the end of the decade. Volvo Group is similarly advancing its hydrogen portfolio and investing significant amounts into hydrogen power solutions such as both fuel-cell and hydrogen-combustion trucks for market rollout towards 2030. Toyota will participate as a technology partner supporting the expansion of hydrogen mobility, leveraging more than 30 years of expertise gained through the development and supply of fuel cell systems, while Bosch is supplying key vehicle components for gaseous hydrogen – with its fuel cell system proven over more than 30 million kilometers on the road – alongside break-through refueling technologies for both liquid and gaseous hydrogen. On the energy and infrastructure side, Volvo Group and Daimler Truck are closely cooperating with energy companies and hydrogen suppliers like Air Liquide, TotalEnergies and MB Energy, and retail operators such as MB Energy and TEAL Mobility (a 50/50 joint venture between TotalEnergies and Air Liquide, operating under TotalEnergies brand). These players are mobilizing their respective capacities to scale both liquid and gaseous hydrogen supply chains. Through their infrastructure investments, they are advancing toward large capacity, high-throughput refueling stations, able to refuel up to 100 trucks per day. They are also leveraging synergies with the fast-growing industrial renewable hydrogen production, driven by the implementation of the European RED III directive. Reaching competitive cost with diesel is essential for fleet operators to adopt hydrogen. Crucially, combining German government policies with industrial collaboration makes this possible through three key levers: Lowering truck cost through incentives and series production. Reaching diesel competitive hydrogen pump price through a more competitive hydrogen supply chain and Greenhouse Gas quota mechanisms. Offering operating incentives like zero emission toll exemptions for fleet operators. Market is rising to meet these conditions. Recent applications under Germany's NOW funding program were oversubscribed, with over 70 high-capacity stations and 800 heavy-duty trucks applied for by industrial companies, confirming strong commercial pull from the logistics sector. While Germany serves as the operational launchpad, demonstrating how industry action and targeted public support can accelerate market development, the industry leaders are calling for strategic measures – supported by national governments and the European Commission – to replicate this model at a continental scale. These measures include scaling infrastructure through synchronized funding calls for refueling stations and vehicles to meet Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) targets; strengthening the commercial viability of hydrogen through pragmatic, harmonized renewable fuel credit mechanisms and toll incentives; and jointly de-risking the overall value chain, from production and liquefaction to final distribution and vehicle operation. This combination of industrial execution and a strong policy framework provides the foundation needed to scale zero-emission freight while reinforcing Europe’s industrial competitiveness, energy resilience and employment, and reducing emissions from freight transport.

articles.title: 29.09.2026 Press release Power Tools New Thermal Camera in Top Performance Class Expert from Bosch Stuttgart / Leinfelden – Making the invisible visible: Professional users can now do this even better than before with the new EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C thermal camera from Bosch. The tool belongs to the Top Performance Class Expert from Bosch, which provides professionals with power tools, measuring technology, and accessories for the highest demands. The EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C is the first thermal camera with an 18V battery from Bosch, making it part of the Professional 18V System , which covers all major applications and, thanks to the multi-brand AmpShare Alliance , even extends beyond Bosch's own product range. Many brands, many tools, one battery system: All tools – from compact screwdrivers to miter saws – can be operated with the same 18V lithium-ion battery and just one charger. This saves users time, space, and money. In addition, Bosch is launching another model, the PRO GTC18V-600-16C.Precisely Detect and Correctly Interpret Temperature Differences As a tool from the Expert top performance class, the EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C offers essential functions for numerous applications: Electricians use it for non-contact testing of control cabinets and connections. In the HVAC sector, users can quickly locate heating pipes, blockages, or leaks. The new thermal camera is also suitable for industrial applications to monitor machinery, in the automotive trade for engine diagnostics, and for energy consultants to analyze building envelopes. The built-in infrared sensor offers a native resolution of 384 x 288 px and covers a temperature range of -30 °C to +650 °C – the largest measuring range among Bosch thermal cameras. The technological highlight is the integrated AI Image Boost technology: A specially trained AI model analyzes the captured thermal imaging data. When this function is activated, the camera calculates an optimized version with four times more measurement points from a frozen thermal image. Compared to conventional tools, the EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C, thanks to the high sensor resolution and activated AI Image Boost, delivers up to eight times more measurement points than the PRO GTC18V-600-16C. This reliably reveals the finest structures and thermal details indoors and outdoors, which allows for even more concrete analyses and helps users interpret the thermal images. Clever functions also support the professional in editing images and capturing and evaluating data directly in the tool. Intuitive Operation and Robust Suitability for Construction Sites The 4.3-inch touchscreen ensures a first-class user experience; alternatively, operation can be carried out via a joypad. Users can set up to five additional measuring points directly on the screen and edit images in the tool or add a voice note. Since harsh conditions prevail on construction sites, the camera has a robust design. A reinforced 360° rubber protection protects the display and housing from impacts. The tool is dust and splash-proof in accordance with protection class IP54 and can withstand drops from up to two meters. To expand the measuring capabilities, the camera has an integrated Type-K interface for external temperature probes, which also are available in various versions from Bosch and enable direct contact measurements. Via the integrated WiFi, data can be sent directly to the Bosch ThermalOn app. Alternatively, the images can be transferred to a computer via USB-C. Whether mobile in the app or on a computer using the free GTC Transfer Software, the images can be further edited, sent, or archived. The thermal cameras EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C and PRO GTC18V-600-16C will be available from November 2026. All prices are recommended retail prices excluding VAT. You can find the tool specifications table in the PDF, see “download”. Subject to change.

articles.title: 21.10.2026 Press release Venture Capital Bosch Ventures invests in Sonexos Stuttgart, Germany / Lausanne, Switzerland – Bosch Ventures is investing in Swiss deep-tech company Sonexos as part of its CHF 5 million Pre-Series A financing round. The round will support the industrialization and market introduction of Sonexos’ novel plasma-based technology for active noise control.Sonexos is developing a new way to tackle one of acoustics’ persistent engineering challenges: low-frequency noise from fans, compressors and motors. Conventional solutions typically require significant space and material and can restrict airflow. Sonexos instead uses an electronically controlled layer of plasma to absorb sound, creating a thin, lightweight solution with no moving parts.Deep tech with industrial relevance and societal impactFor Bosch Ventures, Sonexos brings together differentiated deep technology, industrial relevance and the potential to improve everyday life, a strong expression of Bosch’s “Invented for life” principle.“Technology is most valuable when it moves out of the laboratory and solves problems people experience every day. Sonexos is a strong example of that principle: outstanding deep tech addressing a very tangible challenge, with applications ranging from the appliances in our homes to the infrastructure powering the digital economy,” says Dr. Ingo Ramesohl, Managing Director of Bosch Ventures. “What convinced us in particular is the credible pathway toward industrial scale.” Swiss Technology for global MarketsSonexos’ technology originated in research at EPFL and combines plasma physics, high-voltage electronics and adaptive control software. Its Plasmacoustic Metalayer™ absorbs acoustic energy directly at a surface instead of relying on conventional bulky passive absorbers or loudspeakers that cancel sound at a particular listening position.Sonexos’ initial target markets include domestic appliances, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) and industrial systems. The company is also expanding into datacenter and energy-storage cooling, where increasingly powerful computing infrastructure is driving demand for both greater cooling capacity and effective noise management. The potential impact extends beyond acoustic performance. More compact noise-control systems can give engineers greater freedom when designing products in which space, weight and airflow are critical constraints. In applications such as data-center cooling, reducing fan noise without obstructing airflow could also help reconcile growing infrastructure needs with the interests of surrounding communities.From breakthrough technology to series production “This investment marks an important step from breakthrough technology toward industrial-scale production,” says Mark Donaldson, Founder and CEO of Sonexos. “Together with our customers and partners, we are now turning plasmacoustics into a technology that can be deployed at scale.”The investment comes at a decisive stage in Sonexos’ development. The company is already conducting paid prototype-integration programs with global manufacturers of domestic appliances and HVAC equipment. The new financing will be used primarily for industrialization, customer programs and the further development of Sonexos’ intellectual-property portfolio.The seed investment in Swiss-based Sonexos underscores Bosch Ventures’ international commitment to advancing deep-tech innovation. Complementing this international investment approach, Bosch Ventures announced its earlier this month, dedicated to investing in German deep-tech startups.
